title: Swap the opencode reviewer for dsh, held read-only by its permission mode
summary: The review roster drops opencode and gains dsh. dsh is no longer launched through `sh -c` with the prompt as an argument: osf starts `dsh --profile headless` directly and writes the prompt to its standard input, so no POSIX shell is needed on any platform. Because dsh keeps a shell, it is now held to read-only file writes by `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=read-only` in its environment, and the review job's network allow-list swaps `openrouter.ai` and `models.opencode.ai` for `api.deepseek.com`. The dsh CI job also checks that the pinned review image carries dsh 0.2.0-rc.2, and the roster, workflow and decision records are updated to match.

flows.title: One dsh review run
flows.summary: How a pull request reaches the dsh reviewer and how its answer comes back: the job starts osf in the pinned image, osf starts dsh directly with the prompt on standard input and the read-only permission mode in the environment, dsh reads the read-only checkout and calls DeepSeek, and prints its answer for the job to save.

messages.label: osf review run --reviewer dsh
messages.note: The job passes only DEEPSEEK_API_KEY into the container and mounts the checkout, the base config and the work item read-only.

messages.label: dsh --profile headless
messages.note: No shell wrapper: osf starts dsh directly and writes the prompt to its standard input, so a platform without a POSIX shell can still start it.

messages.label: DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=read-only
messages.note: The read-only permission mode is set in the child's environment. It refuses file writes and edits, and an escalation finds no approval channel in a headless run.

messages.label: read diff and commit log
messages.note: The prompt names the path of the diff file; dsh reads it and the checkout with its own tools.

messages.label: model calls
messages.note: The only model endpoint the job's allow-list permits; dsh's sandbox does not confine the network, so the allow-list bounds its shell, web and subagent tools.

messages.label: JSON answer on stdout
messages.note: dsh takes no answer-schema flag and no model flag, so the prompt asks for the JSON answer and dsh prints only the final answer on standard output.

messages.label: /out/dsh.json
messages.note: The job uploads the saved answers as the review-run-dsh artifact for the final reduce job.

steps.heading: The roster swaps
steps.body: osf.toml names codex, claude and dsh; opencode is off the list.

steps.heading: A dsh job takes its place
steps.body: The opencode job is gone; review-dsh runs the pinned image and checks its dsh version.

detail.text: The dsh job asks the image for its dsh version and fails unless it matches the pin.

steps.heading: Started directly
steps.body: osf runs dsh --profile headless and writes the prompt to its standard input.

detail.text: The agent table holds the command, and osf starts it with no shell wrapper on any platform.

steps.heading: Held read-only
steps.body: DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=read-only refuses file writes while the shell stays in the tool list.

detail.text: The read-only permission mode is what confines dsh's file writes, since its sandbox does not confine the network.

steps.heading: Bounded by the allow-list

detail.text: The allow-list names api.deepseek.com and blocks every other host, which bounds dsh's shell, web and subagent tools.

steps.heading: The answer comes back
